2101986803766985212.content_en: 'It's an overseas platform, so the tax office won't find out.' This is the most common misunderstanding about affiliate income from overseas FX such as XM, and it is a dangerous assumption. The National Tax Agency actively conducts audits of individuals who trade over the internet and of individuals who invest overseas. Overseas FX affiliate income falls into both. In addition, when remittances above a certain amount arrive from overseas into a Japanese account, the financial institution files an overseas remittance report with the tax office. Moreover, overseas FX affiliate income is more complicated to process than ordinary affiliate income: (1) USD rewards are converted into yen at the rate on the day they arise; (2) the rate difference up to the payment date is handled separately as foreign exchange gain/loss; (3) revenue is recorded in the year the reward was confirmed, not the payment date. In this video I summarized the points that are easy to get wrong about taxes on overseas FX affiliate income. It also touches on the treatment of XM bonuses and points. If your rewards have been growing, please watch!
2101986803766985212.content_original:
海外のプラットフォームだから、税務署には把握されないでしょう。
XMなど海外FXのアフィリエイトで一番多い誤解ですが、これは危険な思い込みです。

国税庁は、インターネット取引を行う個人にも、海外投資を行う個人にも、積極的に税務調査を行っています。
海外FXのアフィリエイトは、この両方に当てはまる領域です。

さらに、海外から日本の口座に一定額を超える送金があると、金融機関から税務署に国外送金等調書が提出されます。

しかも、海外FXアフィリエイトは普通のアフィリエイトより処理が複雑です。

・米ドルの報酬は発生した日のレートで円に換算する
・入金日までのレートの差は為替差損益として別に処理する
・売上は入金日ではなく報酬が確定した日の年に計上する

今回の動画では、海外FXアフィリエイトの税金について、間違いやすいポイントをまとめて解説しました。
XMのボーナスやポイントの扱いにも触れています。

報酬が伸びてきた方は、ぜひご覧ください！

2102709126879146091.content_en: Trading gold on an XM KIWAMI account at 1 lot with 100,000 yen, a stop-out occurs after about $5.5 of adverse movement, so I had Gemini verify against IC and EBC. I thought IC would be the cheapest, but never expected EBC to win outright. EBC fixes leverage at 500x unless it's a special time such as before the weekend close. IC has HMR (margin rule), but it isn't as frequent as Exness, where leverage gets restricted before you notice. I'm concerned about EBC's recent blunder of being expelled from the Financial Commission. IC's weak points are deposits/withdrawals and support. [Corrected comparison table of effective drawdown tolerance and cost (100 oz / 15,000 yen = $1 conversion)] Accounts compared: (1) XM KIWAMI; (2) IC Markets (Raw/MT); (3) IC Markets (cTrader); (4) EBC Financial (PRO). Account funds: XM and IC are 100,000 yen at 1000x leverage; EBC is 500x leverage so 200,000 yen is assumed. Stop-loss (SL rate): XM 20% (9,000 yen remaining); both IC accounts 50% (22,500 yen remaining); EBC 30% (27,000 yen remaining). Initial trading cost (spread + commission): (1) about $1.50 (about 2,250 yen); (2) about $1.20 (about 1,800 yen); (3) about $1.10 (about 1,650 yen); (4) about $0.80 (about 1,200 yen). Effective tolerable loss (balance - cost - SL amount): (1) 88,750 yen; (2) 75,700 yen; (3) 75,850 yen; (4) 171,800 yen. Effective tolerable price range: (1) about $5.91 (measured $5.5-5.6); (2) about $5.04; (3) about $5.05; (4) about $11.45. Total round-trip cost per lot: (1) about $15.00 (2,250 yen); (2) about $12.00 (1,800 yen); (3) about $11.00 (1,650 yen); (4) about $8.00 (1,200 yen). Comparison of tolerance per account (with XM as the baseline): XM (100k / 1,000x / SL 20%) - effective tolerance about $5.5 to 5.9. Because you start in the minus by the spread the moment you enter, it falls short of the theoretical value ($6.07) and is stopped out near $5.5. IC Markets (100k / 1,000x / SL 50%) - effective tolerance about $4.7 to 5.0. Because the stop-out level is a high 50% (a balance of 22,500 yen is required), after deducting spread and commission it goes 0.8-0.9 dollars earlier than XM (below $5 to right around $5). It doesn't hold even $5.5, let alone $6. EBC Financial (200k / 500x / SL 30%) - effective tolerance about $11.0 to 11.4. Leverage drops to 500x (required margin 90,000 yen), but the advantage of raising funds to 200,000 yen is very large. The extremely narrow spread/commission cost (about $0.80) also contributes, and it can withstand about twice XM (the $11 range). Difference in total cost (per entry): EBC Pro about $8.00 (almost half of XM); IC cTrader about $11.00; IC Raw (MT4/5) about $12.00; XM KIWAMI about $15.00. For high-leverage, short-range scalping or tight fund management, the picture is 'XM, which can hold on to the limit with SL 20%' versus 'EBC, which withstands $11 with 200,000 yen funds while keeping trading costs lowest'.
